issues.description: The epsilon-delta formal definition is not part of the AP Calculus AB/BC curriculum (it is explicitly excluded from the AP framework). The advanced tier explanation and the second deep dive center heavily on epsilon-delta. While this is mathematically correct and appropriate for an 'advanced' tier, it could mislead students into thinking they need this for the AP exam.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a brief note such as 'The formal epsilon-delta definition is beyond the AP exam but deepens understanding of what a limit truly means.' to set expectations.

issues.description: The second misconception's socratic_response_md references the epsilon-delta definition, which a novice-level student experiencing this misconception is unlikely to know. The Socratic nudge should meet the student at their level.
issues.suggested_fix: Offer a more intuitive nudge first (e.g., 'Does the sequence 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, ... ever equal 1? Yet we say it approaches 1.') and optionally mention epsilon-delta as a formal backup.

issues.description: The concept is 'Limit Definition' (limits.definition) with no prerequisites, yet several check-for-understanding questions and both application problems test the limit definition of the derivative, which is a separate concept (derivatives.definition). While the connection is valuable, the checks should primarily test the limit concept itself; currently 4 of 6 checks and both applications focus on the derivative.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider adding at least one or two checks that test the core limit idea (e.g., evaluating a basic limit, interpreting a graph with a hole, or one-sided limits) without involving derivatives, so coverage is balanced for the stated concept.

issues.description: The deep dive 'Why a Limit and a Function Value Are Fundamentally Different Ideas' ends with a provocative follow-up about a function discontinuous at every rational — this is interesting but potentially confusing for the target audience without any guidance or answer sketch.
issues.suggested_fix: Either remove the provocative follow-up or add a brief hint (e.g., mention Thomae's function) so the student has a starting point.

issues.description: In the novice explanation (framing_index 0), the maps-app analogy is used in both body_md and intuition_md, making the intuition section feel redundant rather than offering a fresh angle.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a different analogy in one of the two places (the campfire analogy from framing_index 1 would work well, for instance).

summary: Mathematically accurate and pedagogically solid overall; minor issues around AP scope clarity for epsilon-delta content, over-emphasis on derivatives in checks/applications for a 'Limit Definition' concept, and a couple of style/consistency nits.
